content.text:
Nature and science facts about the kangaroo

The kangaroo is a marsupial that raises its baby in a pouch on its belly. The baby (a joey) is born very tiny and grows up safely drinking milk inside its mother's pouch. Instead of walking, it hops along on powerful hind legs to travel far and fast, using its thick, long tail for balance. It's a plant-eater that feeds on grass and lives in groups, and it is the animal that represents Australia.

Parent guide — nurturing curiosity

Try a hopping game and pretend "just like a kangaroo!" Tell your child that "it raises its baby in a pouch (a marsupial)," and finding Australia on a map makes it even more exciting.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. How does a kangaroo raise its baby?
A. In a pouch on its belly. The tiny newborn (a joey) grows up inside the pouch, drinking milk.

Q. Why does a kangaroo hop around?
A. It hops on powerful hind legs to travel far and fast, using its long tail for balance.

Q. How can we observe at home?
A. Pretending with a hopping game, learning that "pouch parenting = marsupial," and finding Australia on a map all work well.
